chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three things make you obese, and three things make you skinny. As for those that make you obese: frequent bathing, smelling good scents, and wearing soft clothes. As for those that make you skinny: frequent eating of eggs, fish, and fresh dates.
The compiler of this book said, may God be pleased with him: What is meant by 'frequent bathing' is entering it every other day, for if he enters it every day, his flesh will diminish.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that make a person obese and the three that make them skinny according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes habits into those that promote robustness (saman) and those that cause emaciation (huzn), highlighting the physical benefits of frequent pigeon consumption, pleasant scents, and soft clothing. The compiler’s note clarifies that 'frequent' bathing refers to every other day, as daily immersion was believed to deplete bodily strength, reflecting the humoral medicine prevalent in early Shia scholarly tradition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-194 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Musa ibn Umar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Ammar, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

Three things will make you obese and three things will make you skinny. The three things which will make you obese are: taking a bath often, smelling good scents and wearing soft robes. The three things that will make you thin are eating a lot of eggs, fish and fresh dates.”
The compiler of the book said, “What is meant by ‘taking a bath often’ is taking a bath every other day. Should you take a bath every day you would lose weight.”
